title: ECO: Energy-Constrained Optimization with Reinforcement Learning for Humanoid Walking

blocks.en: ECO: Energy-Constrained Optimization with Reinforcement Learning for Humanoid Walking

blocks.en: Weidong Huang, Jingwen Zhang, Member, IEEE , Jiongye Li, Shibowen Zhang, Jiayang Wu, Jiayi Wang, Hangxin Liu, Member, IEEE , Yaodong Yang, Member, IEEE , Yao Su, Member, IEEE

blocks.en: Abstract —Achieving stable and energy-efficient locomotion is essential for humanoid robots to operate continuously in realworld applications. Existing model predictive control (MPC) and reinforcement learning (RL) approaches often rely on energyrelated metrics embedded within a multi-objective optimization framework, which require extensive hyperparameter tuning and often result in suboptimal policies. To address these challenges, we propose ECO (Energy-Constrained Optimization), a constrained RL framework that separates energy-related metrics from rewards, reformulating them as explicit inequality constraints. This method provides a clear and interpretable physical representation of energy costs, enabling more efficient and intuitive hyperparameter tuning for improved energy efficiency. ECO introduces dedicated constraints for energy consumption and reference motion, enforced by the Lagrangian method, to achieve stable, symmetric, and energy-efficient walking for humanoid robots. We evaluated ECO against MPC, standard RL with reward shaping, and four state-of-the-art constrained RL methods. Experiments, including sim-to-sim and sim-to-real transfers on the kid-sized humanoid robot BRUCE, demonstrate that ECO significantly reduces energy consumption compared to baselines while maintaining robust walking performance. These results highlight a substantial advancement in energy-efficient humanoid locomotion. All experimental demonstrations can be found on the project website: https://sites.google.com/view/eco-humanoid.
blocks.zh: 摘要 — 实现稳定且高能效的运动对于人形机器人在真实世界应用中持续运行至关重要。现有的模型预测控制（MPC）和强化学习（RL）方法通常依赖于嵌入在多目标优化框架中的能耗相关指标，这需要大量的超参数调优，且往往导致次优策略。为了应对这些挑战，我们提出了 ECO（能量约束优化，Energy-Constrained Optimization），这是一种将能耗相关指标与奖励解耦、并将其重构为显式不等式约束的约束强化学习框架。该方法为能耗成本提供了清晰且可解释的物理表征，从而能够进行更高效且直观的超参数调优以提高能效。ECO 引入了针对能耗和参考运动的专用约束，并通过拉格朗日乘子法强制执行，以实现人形机器人稳定、对称且节能的行走。我们将 ECO 与 MPC、带有奖励塑形的标准 RL 以及四种最先进的约束 RL 方法进行了对比评估。包括在儿童尺寸人形机器人 BRUCE 上的仿真到仿真（sim-to-sim）和仿真到真实世界（sim-to-real）迁移在内的实验表明，与基准方法相比，ECO 在保持鲁棒行走性能的同时显著降低了能耗。这些结果突显了在节能人形机器人运动控制方面的重大进展。所有实验演示均可在项目网站上找到：https://sites.google.com/view/eco-humanoid。

Despite these achievements, energy efficiency still remains a significant bottleneck for humanoid robots. Compared to their biological counterparts [5], humanoid robots require substantially more energy to perform similar tasks, limiting their operational range, endurance, and maximum payload in real-world applications [5, 6].
blocks.zh: 近期人形机器人技术的进展使这些机器人能够执行复杂的动作，例如行走、奔跑、跳跃甚至是移动操作（loco-manipulation）[1–4]。尽管取得了这些成果，能效仍然是人形机器人的一个重大瓶颈。与其生物对应物相比[5]，人形机器人执行类似任务需要多得多的能量，这限制了它们在现实世界应用中的作业范围、续航能力和最大有效载荷[5, 6]。

blocks.en: To improve the energy efficiency of humanoid robots, one promising approach is to leverage reinforcement learning (RL) to optimize the control policy. For instance, Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO)-based frameworks incorporate energyrelated terms into reward functions, such as minimizing joint torques, joint accelerations, and contact forces [7–9]. However,
blocks.zh: 为了提高人形机器人的能效，一种很有前景的方法是利用强化学习（RL）来优化控制策略。例如，基于近端策略优化（PPO）的框架将能耗相关项纳入奖励函数中，例如最小化关节力矩、关节加速度和接触力[7–9]。然而，

blocks.en: to achieve efficient and stable locomotion, these methods often require extensive tuning on the weights of the reward terms regarding energy cost, task completion, and stability. This tuning process is non-intuitive and time-consuming, as (i) the effects of weight configurations are not straightforward, (ii) the training periods—ranging from hours to days—to evaluate a single coefficient choice even with parallel computation [10, 11]. Furthermore, conflicting objectives within the reward terms can result in suboptimal solutions or even convergence failures [12, 13]. For example, the learned policy might prioritize minimizing energy consumption at the cost of stability, resulting in unstable walking, or emphasize stability at the expense of significantly increased energy usage.
blocks.zh: 为了实现高效且稳定的运动，这些方法通常需要对涉及能耗成本、任务完成度和稳定性的奖励项权重进行广泛调优。这一调优过程不仅不直观而且耗时，原因在于：(i) 权重配置的影响并不直接；(ii) 即使采用并行计算，评估单个系数选择的训练周期也长达数小时至数天[10, 11]。此外，奖励项中相互冲突的目标可能导致次优解甚至收敛失败[12, 13]。例如，学到的策略可能会以牺牲稳定性为代价优先最小化能耗，从而导致行走不稳定；或者以大幅增加能耗为代价来强调稳定性。

blocks.en: To simplify the reward tuning process for optimizing energetically efficient locomotion with RL, we propose ECO (Energy-Constrained Optimization). ECO leverages constrained RL formualtion to separate conflicting objectives into distinct rewards and constraints [1, 14, 15]. This separation ensures that critical constraints, such as energy consumption limits, are strictly enforced, while task-related rewards, such as velocity tracking and stability can be optimized without extensive tuning of coefficients. Energy constraint thresholds are identified through a physically intuitive tuning process, incrementally adjusted based on direct energy criteria using a linear search algorithm. We evaluate our approach by comparing four state-of-the-art constrained RL methods and investigating various constraint settings. Our results empirically show that the proposed setup outperforms others in training stability and constraint enforcement. Through extensive experiments on both simulation and hardware platforms, we validate that ECO consistently converges to solutions that minimize energy consumption while ensuring stable and robust walking.
blocks.zh: 为了简化利用强化学习优化高能效运动时的奖励调优过程，我们提出了 ECO（能量约束优化，Energy-Constrained Optimization）。ECO 利用约束强化学习表述将相互冲突的目标分离为独立的奖励和约束[1, 14, 15]。这种分离确保了关键约束（如能耗限制）得到严格执行，而与任务相关的奖励（如速度跟踪和稳定性）无需繁琐调节系数即可进行优化。能耗约束阈值是通过一种具有物理直观性的调优过程确定的，即使用线性搜索算法根据直接能耗标准进行增量调整。我们通过比较四种最先进的约束强化学习方法并研究不同的约束设置来评估我们的方法。我们的结果从经验上表明，所提出的设置在训练稳定性和约束执行方面优于其他方法。通过在仿真和硬件平台上的大量实验，我们验证了 ECO 始终能收敛到在确保稳定和鲁棒行走的同时使能耗最小化的解。

blocks.en: Our main contributions can be summarized as follows:
blocks.zh: 我们的主要贡献可总结如下：

blocks.en: - 1) We propose ECO, a method designed for optimizing the energy efficiency of humanoid locomotion. Rather than balancing energy minimization with other reward terms—such as velocity tracking, motion tracking, and stability—we explicitly treat energy cost as a constraint. This approach provides a clear, interpretable physical meaning of the energy cost, enabling efficient and intuitive hyperparameter tuning focused on energy efficiency.
blocks.zh: - 1) 我们提出了 ECO，一种专为优化人形机器人运动能效而设计的方法。与在最小化能耗与其他奖励项（如速度跟踪、动作跟踪和稳定性）之间进行权衡不同，我们将能耗成本显式地作为约束处理。该方法为能耗成本提供了清晰、可解释的物理含义，从而实现了聚焦于能效的高效且直观的超参数调优。

blocks.en: - 2) We investigate four constrained RL algorithms and also different constraint settings to train the policy. Through extensive simulations, we empirically find that the PPOLagrangian method with the current constraint setup achieves the lowest energy cost with fast and stable convergence. Additionally, instead of manually designing efficient walking, we observe that the resulting policy promotes i) extended knee movements, ii) lighter steps, and iii) reduced body shaking as shown in Fig. 1.
blocks.zh: - 2) 我们研究了四种约束强化学习算法以及不同的约束设置来训练策略。通过大量仿真，我们从经验上发现，采用当前约束设置的 PPO-Lagrangian 方法以快速且稳定的收敛实现了最低的能耗成本。此外，无需人工设计高效行走步态，我们观察到所得到的策略促进了：i) 膝关节充分伸展运动，ii) 更轻盈的步伐，以及 iii) 减少身体晃动，如图 1 所示。

blocks.en: - 3) We carry out real-world validations on the Bruce robot. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work to achieve energy-efficient humanoid walking using constrained RL on a real humanoid robot. Compared to MPC and PPO baselines, ECO demonstrates approximately 6 times lower energy consumption than MPC and 2.3 times lower than PPO, setting a new benchmark for energyefficient humanoid locomotion.
blocks.zh: - 3) 我们在 Bruce 机器人上进行了真实世界验证。据我们所知，这是首个在真实人形机器人上利用约束强化学习实现高能效人形机器人行走的工作。与 MPC 和 PPO 基准相比，ECO 的能耗比 MPC 降低了约 6 倍，比 PPO 降低了约 2.3 倍，为高能效人形机器人运动树立了新的基准。

blocks.en: We organize the remainder of the paper as follows. Sec. II reviews the literature related to this work. Sec. III introduces the preliminaries of RL and constrinted RL formulations. Sec. IV presents the proposed ECO framework in detail. Secs. V and VI show the simulation and experiment result of ECO on BRUCE with comprehensive evaluations and compares with baseline methods. Finally, we discuss and conclude the paper in Secs. VII and VIII.

blocks.en: II. RELATED WORK
blocks.zh: II. 相关工作

blocks.en: A. Energy Optimization in Legged Locomotion
blocks.zh: A. 足式机器人运动中的能量优化

blocks.en: Improving energy efficiency directly helps to extend the endurance of legged robots and prevent actuator overheating, thereby improving the overall performance [6]. For example, passive dynamic walkers can achieve efficient and stable walking through mechanical designs without any actuation [16] or with minimal actuation [17]. However, achieving similar efficiency in more complex legged systems, such as quadrupedal and bipedal robots, remains a challenge. As a unified Trajectory Optimization (TO) framework has been widely used for legged locomotion [18, 19], incorporating energy-related constraints tends to be a potential solution. [20] formulates the TO problem with the cost of transport (CoT) as a constraint, which quantifies the energy expenditure per unit distance. However, using TO to consider complex constraints often results in a high-dimensional and nonconvex landscape, which hinders real-time usage. To simplify the problem, energy constraints are approximated using the norm of joint torques and accelerations [2, 21, 22], or by encouraging specific bioinspired efficient behaviors, such as adaptive center of mass (CoM) height control and rolling contact of the stance leg in gait design [23]. In these methods, energy consumption is only implicitly considered, which often makes it compromised in favor of other task requirements, such as stability and robustness.
blocks.zh: 提高能效直接有助于延长足式机器人的续航时间并防止执行器过热，从而提升整体性能[6]。例如，无动力被动行走机器人可以通过机械设计在无需任何驱动[16]或仅需极小驱动[17]的情况下实现高效稳定的行走。然而，在更复杂的足式系统（如四足和双足机器人）中实现类似的能效仍然是一项挑战。由于统一的轨迹优化（TO）框架已被广泛用于足式运动[18, 19]，引入能量相关的约束往往是一个潜在的解决方案。[20] 将运转成本（CoT，量化单位距离的能量消耗）作为约束条件来构建轨迹优化问题。然而，使用轨迹优化来考虑复杂约束通常会导致高维且非凸的优化曲面，从而阻碍其实时应用。为了简化该问题，通常使用关节力矩和加速度的范数来近似能量约束[2, 21, 22]，或者通过在步态设计中鼓励特定的仿生高效行为（如自适应质心（CoM）高度控制和支撑腿在步态设计中的滚动接触）来进行近似[23]。在这些方法中，能耗仅被隐式考虑，这通常使得能耗在其他任务要求（如稳定性和鲁棒性）面前妥协。

blocks.en: B. Learning for Legged Locomotion
blocks.zh: B. 基于学习的足式机器人运动控制

blocks.en: Given the aforementioned issues, offline learning a locomotion policy with complex rewards can be a promising solution to balance energy-efficiency and robustness in real-time [24–26]. [27] demonstrated sim-to-real learning of multiple bipedal gaits through periodic reward composition. Similarly, [28] extended rapid motor adaptation (RMA) for bipedal locomotion to address challenges such as payloads and slippery surfaces. Other methods also integrated model-based footstep planning with model-free RL to achieve dynamic and efficient walking [29, 30]. However, to avoid disrupting the primary learning goals, energy penalties in the reward function often act as regularizers, with minimal impact on reducing excessive joint torque usage. [31] balanced energy consumption with stability through curriculum learning with symmetric mirror loss. [32] further studied different ways to incorporate symmertry, highlighting how symmetry priors can improve gait robustness and sample efficiency without overly restricting policy exploration. [7] explored efficient quadrupedal gaits with energy-centric rewards. [33–36] train control policies for humanoid locomotion using human motion

blocks.en: C. Constrained Reinforcement Learning
blocks.zh: C. 约束强化学习

blocks.en: Constrained RL, or safe RL, formulates the problem as a constrained Markov decision process (CMDP) [37–40], using cost functions to decouple rewards from constraints. This allows robots to maximize rewards while keeping costs within physically meaningful thresholds. CPO [41] uses second-order optimization to enforce constraints iteratively but struggles with scalability in multi-constraint settings. PPO-Lagrangian (PPO-Lag) [42] enhances PPO with primal-dual updates for better constraint satisfaction and performance. Constraint manifold is defined for safe exploration leading to actions that satisfy corresponding constraints in [43, 44]. However, efficient constraint manifold computation for legged robots with a floating base remains challenging. Constraint-rectified Policy Optimization (CRPO) [45] offers a primal-based framework well-suited for multi-constraint problems, while Interior-point Policy Optimization (IPO) [46] employs log-barrier penalties for feasibility enforcement. [15] extended IPO with a teacherstudent framework, transferring most reward terms into constraints to avoid reward scale tuning, and demonstrated robust performance on legged robots. Penalized Proximal Policy Optimization (P3O) [47] uses clamping penalty functions for constraint enforcement and has shown success in reducing violations ( e.g ., self-collision, joint speed limits) in quadruped locomotion [48]. Despite these advancements, these methods have only been validated on quadruped robots. Applying them to humanoid robots, especially when combining energy consumption with other constraints ( e.g ., self-collision), can overly restrict the search space. Given the smaller convergence region of humanoid robots compared to quadrupeds, rethinking how to select and design constraints and how to select an appropriate optimization method within the constrained RL framework to generate efficient and stable walking performance of humanoid robots remains a critical challenge.
blocks.zh: 约束强化学习（Constrained RL）或安全强化学习（safe RL）将该问题建模为约束马尔可夫决策过程（CMDP）[37–40]，利用代价函数将奖励与约束解耦。这使得机器人在最大化奖励的同时，能够将代价保持在具有物理意义的阈值之内。CPO [41] 使用二阶优化来迭代施加约束，但在多约束环境下的可扩展性较差。PPO-Lagrangian（PPO-Lag）[42] 通过原始-对偶更新增强了 PPO，以实现更好的约束满足度和性能。[43, 44] 定义了用于安全探索的约束流形，从而引导产生满足相应约束的动作。然而，针对具有浮动基座的足式机器人进行高效的约束流形计算仍具挑战性。约束校正策略优化（CRPO）[45] 提供了一种非常适用于多约束问题的基于原始变量的框架，而内点策略优化（IPO）[46] 则采用对数障碍惩罚来保证可行性。[15] 通过教师-学生框架扩展了 IPO，将大多数奖励项转化为约束以避免奖励尺度调优，并在足式机器人上展示了鲁棒性能。惩罚近端策略优化（P3O）[47] 使用截断惩罚函数来执行约束，并在减少四足机器人运动中的违规行为（例如自碰撞、关节速度限制）方面取得了成功[48]。尽管取得了这些进展，这些方法仅在四足机器人上得到了验证。将它们应用于人形机器人，尤其是将能耗与其他约束（例如自碰撞）结合时，可能会过度限制搜索空间。鉴于人形机器人相比四足机器人具有更小的收敛区域，如何重新思考约束的选择与设计，以及如何在约束强化学习框架内选择合适的优化方法以生成人形机器人高效稳定的行走性能，仍是一个关键挑战。

blocks.en: IV. PROPOSED ECO FRAMEWORK
blocks.zh: IV. 所提出的 ECO 框架

blocks.en: In this section, we describe the proposed ECO framework, which aims to minimize energy consumption in humanoid locomotion while ensuring stable and natural leg movements. Both the control policy and reward critic are implemented as fully connected neural networks. As illustrated in Fig. 2, the control policy takes the robot’s proprioception and velocity commands as input and outputs the desired joint positions. We train the policy using PPO-Lagrangian [49] in IsaacGym and deploy it directly on the physical robot. The following subsections introduce the state space, action space, constraints settings, reward settings, and the formulation for constraint policy optimization.
blocks.zh: 在本节中，我们介绍了所提出的 ECO 框架，该框架旨在最小化人形机器人行走的能量消耗，同时确保腿部运动平稳自然。控制策略和奖励 Critic 均实现为全连接神经网络。如图 2 所示，控制策略以机器人的本体感受和速度指令作为输入，并输出期望的关节位置。我们在 IsaacGym 中使用 PPO-Lagrangian [49] 训练策略，并将其直接部署在实体机器人上。以下各小节将介绍状态空间、动作空间、约束设置、奖励设置以及约束策略优化的公式表述。

blocks.en: 1) Constraints Selection Consideration : Since minimizing energy consumption is the main focus of this paper, a naive choice is to mix it with other objectives, such as adherence to task commands, behavior stability, and disturbance rejection. However, regarding energy consumption, we observed that adjusting the reward weights alone for PPO does not lead to convergence within the feasible domain (shown in Sec. V-D1). Consequently, we select energy consumption as a constraint in this optimization process. Additionally, we integrate reference motion (using Mirror Loss as the reference in this paper) as a constraint to encourage natural motions.
blocks.zh: 1) 约束选择考量：由于最小化能耗是本文的主要焦点，一个朴素的选择是将其与其他目标混合，例如对任务指令的遵循、行为稳定性和抗扰动能力。然而，关于能耗，我们观察到仅通过调整 PPO 的奖励权重并不能收敛到可行域内（如第 V-D1 节所示）。因此，我们在此优化过程中将能耗选作一个约束。此外，我们还将参考运动（本文中使用镜像损失 Mirror Loss 作为参考）整合为约束，以促进自然运动。

V-D6, we investigate various constraint settings including the constraints used in [15, 48], and find that the current approach struggles with stable convergence as the number of constraints increases. This may be due to humanoid robots having a much smaller constrained feasible domain than quadrupeds, which makes convergence more challenging in the presence of multiple constraints. Therefore, in this work, we focus on two primary constraints: energy minimization and reference motion tracking for humanoid robots.

blocks.en: A. Robot Platform
blocks.zh: A. 机器人平台

blocks.en: We use the kid-sized humanoid robot BRUCE [3, 56, 57] as an example to demonstrate the performance of the proposed ECO framework. BRUCE is 70 cm tall, weighs 4 . 8 kg , and has a total of 16 DoFs, with 3 per arm and 5 per leg. All leg DoFs are driven by liquid-cooled proprioceptive actuators with peak torque 10 . 5 Nm , while the arm DoFs are driven by Dynamixel servo motors. The PD controller gains for both legs are set as \(\mathbf{K_p}=\textit{diag}(7, 10, 7, 10, 1.5)\) and \(\mathbf{K_d}=\textit{diag}(0.2, 0.4, 0.2, 0.4, 0.08)\) for the hip yaw, hip pitch, hip roll, knee pitch, and ankle pitch joints, respectively.

blocks.en: C. Baselines
blocks.zh: C. 基线方法

blocks.en: For comparison, five baseline approaches are chosen to demonstrate that our proposed ECO framework significantly improves energy efficiency without degenerating the performance of humanoid robots in walking tasks. The MPC baseline uses the state-of-the-art model-based hierarchical method which combines a high-level MPC planner with a simplified model and a low-level whole-body controller with the full-body dynamics [19]. Humanoid-Gym [9] is used as the model-free RL baseline (PPO) for training endto-end locomotion policies in humanoid robots. To facilitate a rigorous comparison with the ECO model, the PPO baseline has been augmented with an energy penalty reward [7], which serves as the constraint within the ECO framework. We selected scales of energy penalty reward \(\mu_e \in \{-0.001, -0.01, -0.1, -0.03, -0.05, -0.08, -0.015, -0.02, -0.025\}\), while all other rewards and scales are aligned with those of ECO as detailed in Tab. I. Additionally, a mirror loss is included in the PPO loss function to encourage symmetry, with a fixed weight of 0.1. Three constrained RL baseline methods are chosen as introduce in Eq. (24). For IPO and P3O, we fine-tune the hyperparameters as follows: \(\kappa_1^{\text{P3O}} = 1.0\), \(\kappa_2^{\text{P3O}} = 1.0\), \(\kappa_1^{\text{IPO}} \in \{1.0, 10.0\}\), and \(\kappa_2^{\text{IPO}} = 1.0\).

blocks.en: Regarding the reference motion constraint (Fig. 3(b)), IPO, P3O, and CRPO rapidly converge to the predefined threshold of \(0.05\), though their resulting behaviors are more conservative than those of ECO. In contrast, PPO with various energy coefficients converges to different levels of mirror cost (Fig. 4(b)), often yielding asymmetric and unstable gaits. These results highlight that constrained RL offers a more principled and efficient framework for aligning policy behaviors with target objectives without heavy hyperparameter tuning.
blocks.zh: 关于参考运动约束（图 3(b)），IPO、P3O 和 CRPO 迅速收敛到预定义的阈值 \(0.05\)，但其产生的行为比 ECO 更为保守。相比之下，采用不同能量系数的 PPO 收敛到不同水平的镜像代价（图 4(b)），往往导致不对称和不稳定的步态。这些结果表明，约束强化学习提供了一个更加规范和高效的框架，无需繁重的超参数调优即可使策略行为与目标对齐。

blocks.en: Finally, we note that PPO, P3O, and IPO rely on fixed constraint coefficients (\(\mu_e\), \(\kappa^{\text{P3O}}\), \(\kappa^{\text{IPO}}\)), and CRPO lacks constraint-specific parameters altogether. These approaches are therefore prone to convergence issues or require careful manual tuning. In contrast, ECO leverages PPO-Lag to dynamically update the Lagrange multipliers \(\lambda_i\) using the Adam optimizer, allowing adaptive scaling the impact of constrains during training. This dynamic adjustment significantly improves convergence stability and highlights PPO-Lag as a more effective strategy for optimizing energy-efficient humanoid locomotion.
blocks.zh: 最后，我们注意到 PPO、P3O 和 IPO 依赖于固定的约束系数（\(\mu_e\), \(\kappa^{\text{P3O}}\), \(\kappa^{\text{IPO}}\)），而 CRPO 则完全缺少针对特定约束的参数。因此，这些方法容易出现收敛问题或需要仔细的手动调优。相比之下，ECO 利用 PPO-Lag 使用 Adam 优化器动态更新拉格朗日乘子 \(\lambda_i\)，从而在训练期间能够自适应缩放约束的影响。这种动态调整显著提高了收敛稳定性，并凸显了 PPO-Lag 作为优化高能效人形机器人运动的更有效策略。

blocks.en: 2) Sim-to-Sim Transfer : To evaluate the robustness and generalizability of the learned policy, we transferred it to two additional simulation environments, MuJoCo [61] and Gazebo [62], to assess ECO’s sim-to-sim performance and benchmark it against baseline methods. As shown in Fig. 5(a), our method achieves stable walking across three simulation environments. Fig. 5(b) and (c) demonstrate that ECO consistently maintains a similar gait pattern during cross-simulator transfer and reduces energy usage in Gazebo while BRUCE walks at \(0.1m/s\) over a \(10s\) period. Fig. 5(d) further shows that our method accurately tracks linear velocity commands at three different target speeds (\(0.1m/s, 0.15m/s, 0.2m/s\)) in MuJoCo. We report summary statistics over 10 runs in Tab. IV.

blocks.en: Results show that MPC incurs the highest energy cost and fails to track higher target speeds (e.g., \(0.2m/s\)), likely due to its QP solver being unable to resolve contact dynamics in finite time. PPO exhibits better performance than MPC but with moderate energy consumption. ECO, in contrast, not only achieves accurate velocity tracking but also maintains significantly lower energy consumption—approximately 3 times lower than MPC and 1.4 times lower than PPO.
blocks.zh: 结果表明，MPC 的能耗最高，并且无法跟踪较高的目标速度（例如 \(0.2m/s\)），这可能是因为其 QP 求解器无法在有限时间内求解接触动力学。PPO 的性能优于 MPC，但能耗居中。相比之下，ECO 不仅实现了精确的速度跟踪，而且保持了显著更低的能耗——大约比 MPC 低 3 倍，比 PPO 低 1.4 倍。

blocks.en: in Gazebo. External forces are applied at the origin of the coordinate frame attached to BRUCE’s body link. The timing is chosen as vulnerable transitions from a double-stance phase to lifting the left foot or the right foot. Since the response to perturbations varies with the direction in these two cases, we record the maximum force BRUCE could resist for both timings and use the smaller of the two values for analysis. As shown in Fig. 6, the proposed ECO framework demonstrates greater robustness across all directions, especially in the sagittal direction, compared to the baseline MPC, and shows comparable robustness to PPO. Although ECO has not encountered pushes with a duration longer than \(0.001s\) in the training stage, ECO still performs well under longer pushes, indicating that our method has not overfitted to improve energy efficiency in compromise of robustness. Besides controlled pushes, two qualitative disturbance experiments in Mujoco are conducted to evaluate robustness under more diverse and unpredictable scenarios: (1) different links of BRUCE are manually dragged at random timings with random magnitudes, producing varied disturbance directions and intensities; (2) Balls are thrown to BRUCE with random velocities to create different impulsive contacts. As shown in the accompanying video, ECO successfully maintains stable walking and recovers from these random perturbations, further demonstrating that the learned policy generalizes beyond the specific disturbance patterns used in training.

blocks.en: 4) Energy Constraint Threshold Analysis : We observe that the baseline method PPO converges (achieving a normalized episode length of \(0.9\)) within 1500 training iterations while consuming approximately \(100J\) of energy with the target walking velocity as \(0.1m/s\). Based on this, we conduct a linear search over energy thresholds of \(20J,40J,60J,80J\), and \(100J\) to identify the minimum threshold that enables the policy to achieve similar normalized episode length within 1500 iterations, as shown in Fig. 7. The \(60J\) threshold provides the best trade-off between energy efficiency and locomotion stability. This approach is effective as it leverages physically meaningful thresholds while supporting parallel evaluation. A finer-grained search (e.g., with \(10J\) increments) can discover policies with even lower energy consumption (e.g., \(50J\)) that still maintain stability. If further energy reduction is required, smaller step sizes enable finer control at the cost of additional computation.
blocks.zh: 4) 能耗约束阈值分析：我们观察到基线方法 PPO 在 1500 次训练迭代内收敛（达到 \(0.9\) 的归一化回合长度），同时在目标行走速度为 \(0.1m/s\) 时消耗约 \(100J\) 的能量。基于此，我们在 \(20J\)、\(40J\)、\(60J\)、\(80J\) 和 \(100J\) 的能量阈值上进行线性搜索，以确定使策略能够在 1500 次迭代内达到类似归一化回合长度的最小阈值，如图 7 所示。\(60J\) 阈值在能效与运动稳定性之间提供了最佳折衷。该方法非常有效，因为它利用了具有物理意义的阈值，同时支持并行评估。更细粒度的搜索（例如以 \(10J\) 为增量）可以发现能耗更低（例如 \(50J\)）且仍能保持稳定性的策略。如果需要进一步降低能耗，更小的步长能够实现更精细的控制，但代价是增加计算量。

blocks.en: A. Real World Results

blocks.en: To verify the improvement in energy efficiency, we deploy the learned policy from ECO, along with the two baseline methods, on the real robot hardware BRUCE for comparison. Statistical results across multiple experiment runs, including the linear velocity along the x direction (speed), the total motor power (energy), and the body height in the world frame, are reported in Tab. V. Due to the sim-to-real gap, velocity tracking on the hardware is less accurate than in simulation. To ensure a fair comparison of energy consumption, we select three sets of data with similar, though not identical, speeds from multiple experiments using different methods. As shown in Fig. 10(a), ECO consistently maintains motor power near or below the energy cost threshold \(2.5W(60J/24s)\)—approximately 6 times lower than MPC and 2.3 times lower than PPO according to the cumulative energy graph. Moreover, with the learned policy from ECO, BRUCE successfully rejects disturbances and traverses different outdoor terrains as illustrated in Fig. 11. The full hardware demonstration clips including comparisons with baselines, disturbance rejection, and outdoor walking can be seen in the accompanying video.

blocks.en: B. Emergent Behaviors
blocks.zh: B. 涌现行为

blocks.en: Empirical studies indicate that straight knee and heel-to-toe walking enhance energy efficiency in humans and humanoid robots [23, 63]. Instead of manually designing these behaviors for efficient locomotion, ECO shows that minimizing energy consumption can generate similar behaviors without explicit prescriptions, which also demonstrates that these bio-inspired behaviors are related to energy efficiency.
blocks.zh: 实证研究表明，直膝和由脚跟到脚尖（heel-to-toe）的行走方式可以提高人类和人形机器人的能效 [23, 63]。ECO 没有为了高效运动而手动设计这些行为，而是表明最小化能耗可以在没有明确规定的情况下生成类似的行为，这也证明了这些仿生行为与能量效率密切相关。

blocks.en: Fig. 12 illustrates the joint-level behaviors during walking. Fig. 12(a) compares the left knee joint angle over time, where ECO demonstrates a less flexed knee compared to MPC and PPO. In Fig. 12(b), the torque applied to the left knee joint is compared. ECO consistently requires lower torque to maintain stability and velocity tracking, resulting in reduced energy expenditure during walking. Due to the lack of precise forcetorque sensors under the feet of BRUCE, the knee torques can also implicitly serve as a measure of the intensity of ground contact as the knee exerts the most force in humanoid locomotion. Additionally, we compare the body oscillation over a \(10s\) stable walking period. Fig. 10(b) shows that BRUCE exhibits fewer oscillations with a lower frequency and smaller magnitude when walking with the policy from ECO, compared to MPC and PPO. The less body oscillation and smaller knee torques suggest that improved energy efficiency also results in lighter steps and reduced stomping.

blocks.en: VII. DISCUSSION
blocks.zh: VII. 讨论

blocks.en: A. Rewards v.s. Constraints
blocks.zh: A. 奖励与约束

blocks.en: In this study, we find that tuning reward scales through hyperparameter search within the RL framework (PPO) is an inefficient approach to reducing energy consumption in humanoid robots. This inefficiency arises because reward scales do not correspond linearly to physical quantities, demanding a delicate balance between meeting energy requirements, following task commands, and maintaining motion stability. In contrast, constrained RL explores a space defined by explicit constraints, many of which have direct physical significance, such as energy consumption limits and joint restrictions. This makes tuning constraints more straightforward and effective compared to adjusting reward or loss weights.
blocks.zh: 在本研究中，我们发现在强化学习框架（PPO）内通过超参数搜索调整奖励尺度对于降低人形机器人的能耗是一种低效的方法。这种低效性源于奖励尺度与物理量之间不存在线性对应关系，需要在满足能量需求、遵循任务指令和保持运动稳定性之间进行微妙的权衡。相比之下，约束强化学习（constrained RL）探索由显式约束所定义的空间，其中许多约束具有直接的物理意义，例如能耗限制和关节约束。与调整奖励或损失权重相比，这使得调整约束更加直接且有效。

blocks.en: In this work, we try to incorporate self-collision, foot contact velocity, and foot clearance as additional constraints. First, the cost terms associated with different constraints often differ in magnitude, which can lead to imbalanced gradient updates when training the multi-head cost critic [15]. As a result, costs with smaller magnitudes—such as the self-collision cost in Fig. 9(f)—tend to converge more slowly. This issue could be mitigated by applying appropriate normalization techniques [64] to rescale cost signals to comparable magnitudes. Second, accurately predicting different types of costs may require heterogeneous information. For instance, inferring self-collision from the current privileged observation (i.e., joint angles and base-link kinematics) is particularly challenging, as it requires the network to implicitly reconstruct the geometry of the body in the world frame from joint-centric data. This suggests that a richer observation space—including world-frame information—or a specialized cost critic for self-collision may be necessary to improve both prediction accuracy and constraint satisfaction.

We believe further study is required to handle a larger number of constraints in humanoid locomotion. For instance, incorporating model-based prior knowledge to refine the search space—such as using nullspace projections to prioritize control tasks, as commonly done in the control community [65]—could help in selecting appropriate constraints and mitigating task conflicts. blocks.en: B. Optimization Method Selection
blocks.zh: B. 优化方法选择

blocks.en: Our experiments show that among the four constrained RL algorithms, PPO-Lag is the most effective. CRPO, as a primal algorithm, does not introduce additional dual variables for optimization and involves fewer hyperparameters, making it theoretically simpler and easier to implement compared to primal-dual methods. However, it lacks the smooth transition between reward and constraint optimization objectives that primal-dual methods offer, making it difficult to achieve stable convergence in humanoid robots. P3O uses clamping functions on constraints to apply a linear cost gradient penalty until the constraints are met. However, this linear penalty makes balancing multiple constraints difficult, as each constraint has distinct physical significance and magnitude, requiring separate coefficients \(\kappa_i^{\text{P3O}}\). Small coefficients lead to slow convergence, while large ones make the system overly conservative. IPO, as a method that theoretically also employs penalty functions, exhibits performance similar to P3O in our experiments. It also requires careful tuning of the coefficient \(\kappa_i^{\text{IPO}}\) to balance constraints effectively.
blocks.zh: 我们的实验表明，在四种约束强化学习算法中，PPO-Lag 是最有效的。CRPO 作为一种原始（primal）算法，在优化中不引入额外的对偶变量，且涉及的超参数较少，与原始-对偶方法相比在理论上更简单且更易于实现。然而，它缺乏原始-对偶方法所提供的在奖励和约束优化目标之间的平滑过渡，导致在人形机器人上难以实现稳定收敛。P3O 在约束上使用截断函数施加线性代价梯度惩罚，直至满足约束。然而，由于每个约束具有不同的物理意义和量级，需要独立的系数 \(\kappa_i^{\text{P3O}}\)，这种线性惩罚使得平衡多个约束变得困难。较小的系数导致收敛缓慢，而较大的系数则使系统过于保守。IPO 作为一种理论上也采用惩罚函数的方法，在我们的实验中表现出与 P3O 相似的性能。它同样需要仔细调整系数 \(\kappa_i^{\text{IPO}}\) 以有效平衡约束。

blocks.en: In contrast, ECO leverages PPO-Lag to update both the Lagrange multipliers and the policy, allowing the Lagrange multipliers and their learning rates to adapt to the magnitude of each constraint. By utilizing the Adam optimizer to update these multipliers and learning rates, ECO effectively adapts to each constraint while smoothly transitioning the optimization objective between rewards and constraints. As a result, ECO achieves stable convergence in humanoid robots.
blocks.zh: 相比之下，ECO 利用 PPO-Lag 同时更新拉格朗日乘子和策略，使得拉格朗日乘子及其学习率能够自适应每个约束的量级。通过利用 Adam 优化器来更新这些乘子和学习率，ECO 在奖励与约束之间平滑过渡优化目标的同时，有效地适应了每个约束。因此，ECO 在人形机器人上实现了稳定收敛。

blocks.en: However, ECO faces challenges in optimizing the five constraints considered in our study, highlighting the need for improved optimization techniques in future work. Leveraging the dynamics model of humanoid robots to improve the convergence of constrained RL within a restricted feasible region could be a promising direction [13, 66, 67].
blocks.zh: 然而，ECO 在优化我们研究中考虑的五个约束时面临挑战，突显了未来工作中需要改进优化技术。利用人形机器人的动力学模型来改善约束强化学习在受限可行域内的收敛性可能是一个有前景的方向 [13, 66, 67]。

blocks.en: C. Sim-to-Real Failure Cases
blocks.zh: C. 仿真到真实失败案例

blocks.en: Our methods successfully transfer to the real world, and we identify several key factors that critically affect policy transfer:
blocks.zh: 我们的方法成功迁移到了真实世界，并且我们确定了几个对策略迁移产生关键影响的重要因素：

blocks.en: - 1) PD Gain Tuning : We find that carefully tuning the proportional (\(K_p\)) and derivative (\(K_d\)) gains of the lowlevel PD controller is essential to align the joint-position tracking performance between simulation and hardware. Otherwise, differences in system dynamics can cause the policy to produce divergent behaviors in the real world.
blocks.zh: - 1) PD 增益调优：我们发现，仔细调整底层 PD 控制器的比例增益（\(K_p\)）和微分增益（\(K_d\)）对于对齐仿真与硬件之间的关节位置跟踪性能至关重要。否则，系统动力学的差异会导致策略在真实世界中产生发散行为。

blocks.en: - 2) Compliant ankle strategy : We find that high PD gains at the ankle lead to instability upon ground contact due to sensor noise. To address this, we reduce the ankle’s PD gains, making the joints more compliant and the policy less sensitive to noise. This simple adjustment significantly enhances robustness to terrain variations and modeling errors in real-world tests.
blocks.zh: - 2) 柔顺脚踝策略：我们发现脚踝处过高的 PD 增益会因传感器噪声而在触地时导致不稳定。为了解决这个问题，我们降低了脚踝的 PD 增益，使关节更加柔顺，策略对噪声更不敏感。这种简单的调整显著增强了在真实世界测试中对地形变化和建模误差的鲁棒性。

blocks.en: - 3) Sensor Noise and Bias : Real sensors exhibit both highfrequency noise (especially in joint-velocity measurements) and low-frequency biases (e.g. Euler-angle drift
blocks.zh: - 3) 传感器噪声与偏差：真实传感器同时存在高频噪声（特别是在关节速度测量中）和低频偏差（例如欧拉角漂移

blocks.en: upon reset). To account for this, we inject noise and random biases—matched in magnitude to hardware measurements—into the corresponding state observations during domain randomization.
blocks.zh: 重置时）。为了解决这一问题，我们在域随机化过程中，向相应的状态观测中注入噪声和随机偏置——其幅值与硬件实测值相匹配。

blocks.en: D. More complex settings
blocks.zh: D. 更复杂的设置

blocks.en: While our method is effective for stable walking, applying it to more complex scenarios, such as transitioning from flat surfaces to stairs, presents new challenges. For instance, a lower foot lift is energy-efficient on flat surfaces, but stair climbing requires higher foot lifts and precise planning to navigate varying stair heights efficiently. One possible extension is to introduce mode-aware constraints [68, 69] that adapt according to different terrains and command types. For example, energy constraints could be relaxed when stair climbing is anticipated. A terrain classifier or visual encoder [70–72] could be used to identify terrain types, allowing the policy to dynamically adjust constraint thresholds accordingly. In addition, modelbased planning [13, 73, 74] can be incorporated, in which a high-level planner selects locomotion modes based on the environment, while the low-level control executes constrained locomotion policy conditioned on the selected mode. This hierarchical approach aligns well with the constrained RL framework, as constraints can be defined and enforced differently across modes. We consider this an exciting future direction and plan to explore model-based extensions in our follow-up work.
blocks.zh: 虽然我们的方法在实现稳定行走方面行之有效，但将其应用于更复杂的场景（例如从平地过渡到楼梯）时会带来新的挑战。例如，较低的抬脚高度在平地上具有较高的能量利用效率，但爬楼梯需要更高的抬脚高度和精确的规划，以便高效应对不同高度的台阶。一种可能的拓展是引入模式感知约束 [68, 69]，使其能够根据不同的地形和指令类型进行自适应调整。例如，当预期要爬楼梯时，可以放宽能量约束。可以使用地形分类器或视觉编码器 [70–72] 来识别地形类型，从而允许策略据此动态调整约束阈值。此外，还可以结合基于模型的规划 [13, 73, 74]，由上层规划器根据环境选择运动模式，而底层控制则执行以所选模式为条件的受约束运动策略。这种分层方法与受约束强化学习框架高度契合，因为约束可以在不同模式之间进行差异化的定义和施加。我们认为这是一个令人振奋的未来方向，并计划在后续工作中探索基于模型的扩展。

blocks.en: VIII. CONCLUSION
blocks.zh: VIII. 结论

blocks.en: In this paper, we optimize the energy consumption for humanoid walking through constrained RL by separating energy consumption and reference motion objectives from the reward function. We demonstrate that the ECO framework can converge to a policy that achieves lower energy consumption while maintaining robustness. Meanwhile, ECO is resilient to hyperparameter settings, thereby eliminating the need for extensive tuning on the weights of rewards. Extensive experiments in both simulation and real-world hardware validate that our approach can significantly improve the energy efficiency of humanoid walking without compromising robustness.
blocks.zh: 在本文中，我们通过受约束强化学习优化仿人机器人行走的能耗，将能耗和参考运动目标从奖励函数中分离出来。我们证明了 ECO 框架能够收敛到一种在保持鲁棒性的同时实现更低能耗的策略。同时，ECO 对超参数设置具有较强的适应性，从而无需对奖励权重进行大量调优。在仿真和真实硬件上的大量实验验证了我们的方法能够在不牺牲鲁棒性的情况下显著提高仿人机器人行走的能量效率。

blocks.en: Yaodong Yang (Member, IEEE) received the bachelor’s degree from the University of Science and Technology of China, the MSc degree from Imperial College London, and the PhD degree from University College London (nominated by UCL for Joint AAAI/ACM SIGAI Doctoral Dissertation Award). He is an assistant professor with Institute for AI, Peking University. Before joining Peking University, he was an assistant professor with King’s College London. He studies game theory, reinforcement learning and multi-agent systems, aiming to achieve artificial general collective intelligence through multi-agent reinforcement learning. He has maintained a track record of more than sixty publications at top conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, etc) and top journals (Artificial Intelligence, National Science Review, etc), along with the best system paper award at CoRL 2020 and the best blue-sky paper award at AAMAS 2021. He was awarded ACM SIGAI China Rising Star and World AI Conference (WAIC’22) Rising Star.
